newsitem.title: USA: Boeing rejects union proposal on making doors.
newsitem.headline: Boeing rejects union proposal on making doors.

text.p: Boeing Co on Friday said it has rejected a union proposal that would have retained the production of airplane doors at Boeing.
The move will result in the reassignment of about 180 employees.
Boeing has decided to place the door production with an outside contractor, but no layoffs will occur, the company said in a statement.
The workers, who are represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers (IAM/AW), are based in Renton, Wash., and Wichita, Kan.

After researching pressurized door production for two years, Boeing had advised the union it would outsource their manufacturing. But on December 5, the union suggested alternatives that would lead to the retention of work, Boeing said.
The proposal, including the formation of an Integrated Product Team with union leaders as members, would conduct another six-month study and make its recommendations.
Boeing said the union proposal did not present any alternatives which were called for in its current contract.
